**Grid:** Under Article B5.5.5 a.i (page 37), if any team personnel are touching an F1 Car, or team equipment is connected to it, after the fifteen-second signal, the driver must start the TTCS from the Pit Lane [E1][E14]. A driver who fails to do so receives a Stop-and-Go Penalty [E1].

**Pit lane Fast Lane:** If personnel are touching a car or equipment is connected to a car in the Fast Lane after that signal, the driver receives a Drive-Through Penalty [E1].

**Driver needing assistance:** The driver must immediately raise their hands above their head. Once the other cars able to leave have left the grid, marshals will push the car into the Pit Lane Inner Lane (per B5.7.1). Marshals with yellow flags stand beside the car to warn drivers behind [E1].

**Precedent:** At the 2026 Australian Grand Prix, the Stewards gave Car 43 (Franco Colapinto, BWT Alpine) a Stop and Go Penalty. A team member was touching the car on the grid after the fifteen-second signal, and the car did not start from the Pit Lane. The Stewards cited a breach of B5.5.5 a) i) [E9].

In the 2022 Sporting Regulations, when the clerk of the course decides it is safe to call in the safety car, the message **"SAFETY CAR IN THIS LAP"** is sent to all Competitors via the official messaging system (Article 55.14, page 62) [E1].

- The safety car's orange lights are also extinguished. This signals that it will enter the pit lane at the end of that lap [E1].
- When a sprint session or race is being resumed after a suspension, the message differs. It is "STANDING START" (Article 58.12, page 66) [E2] or "ROLLING START" (Article 58.13, page 66) [E3], depending on the restart type.

The minimum mass of the car, without fuel, is 800 kg plus the Heat Hazard Mass Increase, at any time during the Competition (Article 4.1, page 47) [E2][E9].

Related adjustments:
- **Heat Hazard Mass Increase (Article 4.7, page 48):** 5 kg applies in a Race or Sprint Session with a declared Heat Hazard. 2 kg applies in Free Practice, Sprint Qualifying or Qualifying with a declared Heat Hazard [E10].
- **Tyre mass (Article 4.3, page 47):** The 800 kg limit is adjusted up or down (rounded to the nearest 1 kg) according to differences in dry-weather tyre set mass between the 2025 Championship and the preceding year's [E2].
- **Tyre fitment for checking (Article 4.1):** If a car isn't fitted with dry-weather tyres when checked, its mass is determined using a set selected by the FIA technical delegate [E2].

Separately, the driver, seat and driving equipment, plus any designated ballast, must total at least 82 kg (Article 4.6.2, page 47) [E1].

Yes. The Stewards granted Car 18 (Lance Stroll) permission to start the 2026 Australian Grand Prix, despite his failing to set a qualifying time within 107% of the fastest Q1 time [E9][E25][E33].

**Basis:** Under Article B2.4.3b, the Stewards have the power to grant permission if circumstances justify it. They may consider factors such as a suitable lap time in another session and the driver's general performance in the Championship [E9].

**Matters raised by Aston Martin:**
- Car 14 (Alonso) showed the AMR26 could qualify within 107% [E9].
- Stroll had completed 859 km in the AMR26 this year, had 178 Grands Prix starts, and had competed in seven Australian Grands Prix (best result 4th in 2023) [E9].
- The team chose not to run Car 18 in qualifying, out of prudence, because of a damaged oil line, so they could investigate further [E9].

The Stewards found these reasons "compelling" and granted permission. The car was to be placed on the grid in accordance with Article B2.5.4 [E9].

Drivers must stay below **1:37.0** between the Safety Car lines (shown on the pit lane drawing) [E10][E18].

This applies to any laps during and after the end of Qualifying, and to reconnaissance laps when the pit exit is opened for the Race. The purpose is to ensure cars are not driven unnecessarily slowly [E10][E18].

The Race Director's Competition Notes add that exceeding the maximum time from the Second Safety Car Line to the First Safety Car Line on any such lap may be deemed going unnecessarily slowly, other than in exceptional circumstances accepted by the Stewards [E9][E17].

This limit is the one set in the Australian Grand Prix notes (Document 22, 6 March 2026) [E10]. It is separate from the Safety Car deployment rules in Article B5.13.2 (page 45), which concern a minimum time and a gap of ten car lengths [E4].

**Competition Notes, General Instructions, item 1 (page 1)**

- Unless the Stewards accept exceptional circumstances, any driver who exceeds the maximum time from the Second Safety Car Line to the First Safety Car Line "may be deemed to be going unnecessarily slowly" [E1].
- This applies on any lap during and after the Qualifying Session, including in-laps and out-laps. It also covers reconnaissance laps when the pit exit is opened for the Race [E1].
- Teams and drivers will be told the maximum time after the second Practice Session [E1].
- It does not supersede Articles B1.8.5 and B4.1.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations, which apply to the entire Circuit, and this includes the pit lane [E1].
- Incidents will normally be investigated after the Qualifying Session or the Race [E1].

The wording is the same in the Azerbaijan V2 notes [E2] and the Australian notes [E3]. The latest version in the evidence is the Azerbaijan V3 [E1]. The evidence does not state a specific penalty or the actual maximum time.
